name: SIPp
what_it_is: SIPp is an open-source SIP protocol test tool and traffic generator that drives and receives SIP calls using XML-based scenario definitions. It supports multiple transport modes, media playback via PCAP, and detailed statistics collection for load testing and functional validation of SIP equipment.
components: XML scenario engine (parses and executes user-defined call flows)
Built-in scenarios: UAC, UAS, UAC with media (PCAP), regexp, branch, 3PCC, out-of-call handler
ncurses screen UI with 9 monitoring views (scenario, statistics, repartition, variables)
PCAP media player (requires libpcap/libnet, compile-time flag USE_PCAP=1)
GNU Scientific Library integration for random pause distributions (USE_GSL=1)
SCTP transport layer (compile-time flag USE_SCTP=1, requires lksctp-tools)
TLS support via OpenSSL >= 1.1.1 or WolfSSL >= 3.15.0
TLS key logging (compile-time flag TLS_KEY_LOGGING=1, writes to SSLKEYLOGFILE path)
Alpine-based Docker image producing a static binary
Debian-based Docker image with optional wolfSSL support
CSV injection file reader for parameterised call data (-inf flag)
protocols: SIP over TCP (mono and multi socket)
SIP over UDP (mono socket, multi socket, per-IP socket)
SIP over TLS / SIPS (mono and multi socket, X.509 CRL support)
SIP over SCTP (mono and multi socket, multihoming, heartbeat)
RFC 2833 DTMF digit sending over RTP
measurement: Successful and failed call counts with granular failure reason counters (UDP retransmit exceeded, unexpected message, regexp mismatch, TCP congestion, timeout on send/recv, etc.)
Response Time Distribution (RTD) timers — start/stop via scenario attributes, dumped to *_rtt.csv
Standard deviation for response time and call length
Per-message counts: sent, received, retransmitted, lost, unexpected — exported via -trace_counts to CSV
Statistics snapshot frequency configurable with -fd option
Exit codes: 0 all calls OK, 1 at least one failed, 97 internal/global timeout, 99 no calls, -1 fatal, -2 socket bind failure
configuration: XML scenario files (-sf flag) or built-in scenario name (-sn flag)
Transport mode selection (-t flag): u1/un/ui UDP, t1/tn TCP, l1/ln TLS, s1/sn SCTP
Target host and port as positional argument or -remote flag
Local bind address (-i) and port (-p), supports IPv6
Call rate (-r), max calls (-m), max simultaneous calls (-l)
CSV injection file for per-call variables (-inf), IP field selector (-ip_field)
TLS certificate/key files (cacert.pem and cakey.pem expected in cwd), CRL via -tls_crl
SSLKEYLOGFILE environment variable for TLS session key logging
Background daemon mode (-bg); graceful stop via SIGUSR1
Statistics dump file (-trace_stat), response-time dump (-trace_rtt), message log (-trace_msg), error log (-trace_err), call debug (-trace_calldebug), screen dump (-trace_screen)
UDP retransmission disable (-nr); per-send retransmission timer via scenario retrans attribute
Build flags: USE_PCAP=1, USE_SCTP=1, USE_GSL=1, BUILD_STATIC=1, TLS_KEY_LOGGING=1, WOLFSSL=1, DEBUG=1, FULL=1
fault_injection: Scenario-driven unexpected message handling: CANCEL sent if no 200 OK yet, BYE if 200 OK received, ACK sent for 4xx/5xx
Retransmission testing: UDP retrans attribute triggers RFC 3261 §17.1.1.2 timer with configurable T1; globally disabled via -nr
TCP disconnect simulation: -max_reconnect controls reconnection attempts; -reconnect_close drops calls on reconnect
Out-of-call message injection: -oocsf / -oocsn overrides default 200 OK response to unmatched Call-IDs
Conditional branching in scenarios (branchc/branchs) allows simulating error response paths (e.g., 403 Forbidden mid-flow)
Regexp-based response validation failure counted as FailedRegexpDoesntMatch / FailedRegexpShouldntMatch — scenario can branch on mismatch
Global call timeout via -timeout_global forces exit code 97
modes: UAC with PCAP media — originates calls with RTP/RFC2833 media replay
3PCC controller — third-party call control coordinating two remotes via inter-SIPp socket
Background daemon (-bg) — detached process, SIGUSR1 for graceful shutdown
Performance/load test mode — ramp up call rate, measure throughput
Regression test mode — fixed call count (-m), exit code signals pass/fail
constraints: A single SIPp instance communicates with exactly one remote host; 3PCC or multi-leg scenarios require multiple SIPp processes
PCAP media playback may not work over IPv6
SCTP is not supported on Cygwin/Windows
TLS requires cacert.pem and cakey.pem present in the working directory; missing files cause startup failure
TLS key logging requires OpenSSL >= 1.1.1 (not supported with WolfSSL)
Static binary build only tested/supported on Alpine Linux
Multi-socket transport modes are limited by OS file descriptor limits (tunable via ulimit); hard cap via -max_socket
No docker-compose file is provided in the repository; Docker support is build-environment only (produces a binary artifact, not a service stack)
Scenario files must conform to sipp.dtd; DTD validation available via dtd_check.sh
C++17 compiler required to build from source (master/3.7.x branch)
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml — Docker is used only as a build environment to produce a static binary, not to run a service stack
No native SIP proxy or registrar included — SIPp tests against an external SUT
No built-in media generation — RTP/media support requires pre-recorded PCAP files and compile-time USE_PCAP=1
No REST or programmatic API — controlled entirely via CLI flags, signals (SIGUSR1/SIGUSR2), and keyboard input
No Windows native build — only Cygwin is supported on Windows, with reduced feature set
